title: Scoped resource ownership
decision: Reuse the renderer scope for native renderer allocations. Register release at acquisition and retain the scope until its owning renderer is destroyed.

checks.claim: Exercises renderer acquisition and cleanup paths.

exceptions: Synchronous drawing stays outside Effect; nonabortable creation must settle under ownership.
gaps: Native GPU behavior still requires browser or device verification.

title: Actor lifecycle and React ownership
decision: Use the existing particle lifecycle owner for renderer initialization, fallback and loss. React retains activation and browser frame ownership.

checks.claim: Covers late acquisition, loss, replay, fallback and teardown.

exceptions: Animation eligibility and renderer availability remain distinct.
gaps: Tests do not establish physical GPU behavior.

title: React restart and observer lifetime
decision: Choose the shared hook whose lifetime matches the task. useAbortableEffect callback changes do not restart work; reactive identity changes need an effect with explicit dependencies.

checks.claim: Documents lifecycle selection and observer readiness requirements; not a runtime check.

exceptions: Feature state and drawing belong to the app; shared hooks own browser subscriptions.
gaps: Hook selection and readiness require review; this catalog does not prove Strict Mode behavior.

title: Shared requests and cancellation
decision: Reuse the typography request owner for metrics. Preserve per-consumer cancellation and its pending-only policy. Search pinned HTTP capabilities before extending the transport.

checks.claim: Exercises sharing, cancellation and retry behavior for metrics requests.

exceptions: This owner uses an injected Promise fetch contract; it is not a universal HTTP adapter.
gaps: Provider behavior and other cache policies require separate checks.

title: Validate external values at entry
decision: Decode external metrics before they reach measurement or caches. Reuse the owning schema and preserve finite-number and positive-units constraints.

checks.claim: Checks acceptance and rejection of metric payloads.

exceptions: Other domains need their own schema rather than reuse of the metrics shape.
gaps: Changes to Schema APIs require the source lookup workflow.

title: Preserve typed failures
decision: Retain failure stage and cause in the owning adapter; recover only the failures the application can handle. Use the installed tagged-error conventions.

checks.claim: Exercises the configured manual tagged comparison rejection.
Exercises request failures through the application owner.

exceptions: UI presentation and framework error contracts may require boundary conversion.
gaps: Lint catches selected syntax, not correctness of recovery or preservation of every cause.

title: Runtime creation and disposal
decision: Keep the sample database runtime behind its existing Promise facade. Isolated owners expose disposal; the host must end the lifetime explicitly.

checks.claim: Exercises lazy initialization and disposal behavior.
Exercises import restrictions for ManagedRuntime and execution imports in apps/**/*-service.ts, while permitting integration facades.

exceptions: The default database facade intentionally owns module-lifetime state.
gaps: Host shutdown wiring is not established by facade tests; SQL authorization is a separate concern.
Destructured or reassigned aliases, variable property names, indirect wrappers and filenames outside apps/**/*-service.ts remain review-only.

title: Application contracts and provider adapters
decision: Keep application job contracts and resource policy with their owner. Supply provider implementations at composition. A cartridge must identify its public contract, resources and removal dependencies.

checks.claim: Exercises workflow behavior through supplied dependencies.
Rejects shared-to-app imports and app imports of private package source.

exceptions: Plain injected interfaces are appropriate at existing Promise boundaries; no mandatory package or Layer migration.
gaps: Import fences do not prove provider interchangeability or that a cartridge can be removed; verify actual replacement callers.

title: Process and script ownership
decision: Keep social-preview orchestration and native process adaptation separate. The lifecycle scope owns teardown; preserve exit status and await shutdown.

checks.claim: Exercises preview resource cleanup through supplied dependencies.

exceptions: Simple filesystem/path operations remain native; the root dev bootstrap retains flock while Execa owns process lifecycle without an Effect platform adapter.
gaps: Process-tree and platform behavior need native verification beyond supplied adapters.

title: Replace resources without losing ownership
decision: Reuse wet-ink resource slots for replaceable GPU textures. Keep candidate ownership during preparation and release superseded resources.

checks.claim: Exercises replacement, rollback and close during preparation.

exceptions: Restoring bindings depends on what the renderer can restore.
gaps: Real GPU binding validity requires browser evidence.

title: Submission acceptance and cancellation
decision: Keep attachment conversion and send identity in their existing coordinators. Clear input only after current accepted completion; preserve content on conversion failure or unconfirmed delivery.

checks.claim: Exercises duplicate suppression, cancellation, failure and late completions.
Exercises acceptance outcomes through the Eve integration boundary.

exceptions: Local cancellation does not undo remote acceptance; Eve retains session streaming and resume ownership.
gaps: Provider delivery guarantees require provider evidence.

title: Source identity and dependency updates
decision: Keep exact source provenance in the existing manifest. Check installed versions and mirrors before using their APIs; assess releases separately and revalidate dependent catalog entries when pins change.

checks.claim: Exercises dirty mirrors, changed pins, moved tags and installed-version mismatches.

exceptions: Source downloads are reference-only and do not authorize dependency upgrades.
gaps: Matching source identity does not prove an agent read or understood it.

title: Bound work before it reaches a provider
decision: Name the producer, queue, active workers and result allocation separately. Bound each relevant stage using measured limits, propagate waiting or refusal to producers, and reserve independent capacity for work that must not starve. Apply result limits before the driver materializes rows.

checks.claim: Review policy only; catalog validation checks its link, not application behavior.

exceptions: Apply within existing Next.js, React and Bun ownership; no automatic migration or dependency addition.
gaps: No universal runtime enforcement or new library API evidence is claimed. Complete the source lookup and behavior verification for the concrete implementation.

title: Retries require identity and a budget
decision: Retry only classified transient failures under a total attempt and time budget. Establish receiver-side idempotency before retrying writes. A timeout means local waiting ended, not that remote execution failed. Treat already-absent cleanup as success only when absence is the promised postcondition.

Retain exhausted work with a deliberate redrive path.

title: Make recovery and overload policies explicit

Model circuit-breaker states and probe admission before introducing one. Recycle bounded resources and verify recovery under load; in-process task ownership does not establish process isolation or durable recovery.
